name: Surgut Khanty
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Csepregi, Marta. 1998. Szurguti osztjak chrestomathia (Studia uralo-altaica supplementum 6). Szeged. Grammar sketch of Surgut Khanty, plausibly covering stress.

new_statements.quote: A szó főhangsúlya általában az első szótagra esik: wŏntəŋ 'erdei', imi 'anyó'. Háromnál többtagú szavakban a harmadik szótagon mellékhangsúly van: ḳåtɣəʌamən 'a mi kettőnk két háza'. Azokban az esetekben, amikor az első szótagban [-tense], a második szótagban [+tense] magánhangzó van, a hangsúly áttolódik a második szótagra: səran 'zürjén', səɣʌam 'menyhalaim', ḳŏrnat 'képpel'.
new_statements.translation: The main stress of the word generally falls on the first syllable: wŏntəŋ 'of the forest', imi 'old woman'. In words of more than three syllables there is a secondary stress on the third syllable: ḳåtɣəʌamən 'the two houses of the two of us'. In those cases where the first syllable contains a [-tense] vowel and the second syllable a [+tense] vowel, the stress shifts to the second syllable: səran 'Zyrian (Komi)', səɣʌam 'my burbots', ḳŏrnat 'with a picture'.
new_statements.citation: Csepregi, Márta. 1998/2011. Szurguti osztják chrestomathia (Studia uralo-altaica supplementum 6). Szeged: JATE Finnugor Tanszék; 2011 revised edition (rev. Csepregi Márta, Gugán Katalin, Kováts Zsófia), PDF distributed by the LMU Ob-Ugric database.
new_statements.locator: Sec. 1.3 'Hangsúly, intonáció', p. 14 of the 2011 revised edition (PDF page 14; the 1998 print pagination may differ)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default main stress on the first syllable; when the first-syllable vowel is reduced ([-tense], schwa-type) and the second-syllable vowel is full ([+tense]), main stress moves to the second syllable. Full vs. reduced vowel quantity is the conditioning factor, so the pattern is quantity-sensitive with an initial default (the same author's 2017 Russian edition, p. 58, gives only 'main stress mostly on the first syllable' and omits the shift rule, which would read as fixed-initial).
new_statements.secondary_stress: 1998/2011 p. 14: secondary stress on the third syllable in words of more than three syllables (ḳåtɣəʌamən). 2017 p. 58: 'Последующие нечетные слоги несут на себе второстепенное ударение' (following odd-numbered syllables carry secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: Reduced V1 + full V2 words take second-syllable stress (səran, səɣʌam, ḳŏrnat). 2017 ed. p. 58 adds: stress is not phonemic ('не имеет фонематического значения'); Russian loans are stressed either on the first syllable or where Russian stresses them; p. 59: in connected speech semantic/expressive factors can change phrasal and word stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress ('a szó főhangsúlya'), cited forms are isolated words; sentence intonation treated separately (falling; stressed syllables of emphasised words pitched higher; steep fall on the questioned word). Reading confidence is medium because the two editions by the same author differ on whether the second-syllable shift exists.
new_statements.identity_note: Csepregi's chrestomathy describes Surgut Khanty proper (surg1248; the 2017 edition names the Lyamin, Pim, Tromagan, Agan, Little/Big Yugan, Salym and Demyanka varieties, with A. S. Pesikova as native consultant/editor). Filchenko 2007, which Glottolog's bibliography Vasjugan Khanty vasj1234, a dialect of Vach-Vasjugan fare1244), not Surgut; its stress description (initial default, second-syllable stress with reduced V1 + full V2, multiple stresses) nevertheless parallels Csepregi's.

sources.note: Sec. 1.3 'Hangsúly, intonáció', p. 14: main word stress generally on the first syllable; secondary stress on the third syllable in words of more than three syllables; stress shifts to the second syllable when syllable 1 has a [-tense] vowel and syllable 2 a [+tense] vowel (səran, səɣʌam, ḳŏrnat); sentence intonation falling.

sources.citation: Чепреги, Марта. 2017. Сургутский диалект хантыйского языка / под ред. Н. Б. Кошкаревой; ред. хантыйского текста А. С. Песикова; пер. Т. А. Ефремова. Ханты-Мансийск: ООО «Печатный мир г. Ханты-Мансийск» (Обско-угорский институт прикладных исследований и разработок). 275 pp. In Russian.
sources.note: Sec. 1.4 'Ударение, интонация', pp. 58-59: 'Главное ударение в основном падает на первый слог: вӧнтəӈ, ими. Последующие нечетные слоги несут на себе второстепенное ударение: ӄотҳəԓамəн.' Stress is not phonemic; Russian loans stressed on syllable 1 or as in Russian; phrase-level factors may alter word stress. The second-syllable shift rule of the 1998/2011 edition is not repeated here. (PDF text is in a shifted-Cyrillic font encoding; decoded copy saved as and page images p-058/ checked.)

sources.citation: Filchenko, Andrey Y. 2007. A grammar of Eastern Khanty. PhD dissertation, Rice University. xxvi+588 pp. hdl:1911/20605 (Glottolog bib id 22080 files it under surg1248; the abstract says it describes the Vasyugan and Alexandrovo dialects).
sources.note: Sec. 1.7 'Stress', pp. 57-60: 'Stress in Eastern Khanty is dynamic. In bi- or poly-syllabic words, the stress is often assigned to the word-initial syllable'; second-syllable stress when syllable 1 has a reduced vowel (or is closed) and syllable 2 a full vowel; polysyllables carry multiple stresses (1st+3rd or 2nd+4th); trisyllables fluctuate; stress not phonologically relevant (no minimal pairs). Vasyugan/Alexandrovo, not Surgut proper.
